description: Published values used as the Phase 0 acceptance gate. Unless a check says otherwise, values come from the FlyWire network-statistics paper (Lin, Yang, Dorkenwald et al., Nature 634:153-165, 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07968-y), which analysed connectome snapshot v630 (127,978 neurons) with connections thresholded at 5 synapses. The canonical dataset here is v783 (139,255 neurons), so every comparison states its version relationship and a tolerance that accounts for it. Version-independent checks (convention validation) carry tight tolerances; version-sensitive checks carry wider ones and are marked advisory.

network_paper.citation: Lin A., Yang R., Dorkenwald S. et al. Network statistics of the whole-brain connectome of Drosophila. Nature 634, 153-165 (2024)
network_paper.conventions: connections thresholded at five synapses per connection; autoregressive connections are there; reciprocity excludes autapses

flagship_paper.citation: Dorkenwald S. et al. Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. Nature 634, 124-138 (2024)

data_release.note: FlyWire Whole-brain Connectome Connectivity Data, version 783, CC-BY-4.0

codex.note: v783 dataset card reports 139,255 neurons and 3,732,460 connections; see the unresolved_convention_note check

checks.name: n_neurons
checks.source: flagship paper / v783 release
checks.comment: exact: the proofread root-id array defines the neuron set

checks.name: mean_synapses_per_connection
checks.source: network paper (v630), 'the average connection consists of 12.6 synapses'
checks.comment: strongest available validation that the 5-synapse convention and neuropil-level aggregation are correct

checks.name: connection_reciprocity
checks.source: network paper Table 2 (v630)
checks.comment: p_rec = P[beta->alpha | alpha->beta], autapses excluded, 5-synapse threshold

checks.name: clustering_coefficient
checks.source: network paper Table 2 (v630); the same paper also quotes 0.0463
checks.comment: global clustering on the undirected autapse-free projection; tolerance spans both quoted values

checks.name: n_connections_v630_convention
checks.source: network paper (v630, 5-synapse threshold, 127,978 neurons)
checks.comment: v783 has 8.8% more neurons, so a few percent more connections is expected

checks.name: mean_out_degree
checks.source: network paper (v630): 'average in/out-degree of an intrinsic neuron is 20.5'
checks.comment: ours is computed over all neurons with any connection, not intrinsic neurons only

checks.name: scc_size_absolute
checks.source: network paper (v630): giant SCC = 93.3% of 127,978 neurons = 119,404
checks.comment: compared in absolute neurons, not as a fraction: v783 adds ~11k sparsely connected neurons that sit outside the giant SCC, which shifts the fraction without changing the component itself

checks.name: wcc_size_absolute
checks.source: network paper (v630): giant WCC = 98.8% of 127,978 neurons = 126,442
checks.comment: absolute comparison for the same reason as scc_size_absolute

checks.name: scc_fraction
checks.source: network paper (v630): giant SCC holds 93.3% of neurons
checks.comment: version-sensitive: v783 has a larger denominator, so this fraction is expected to be lower than v630's while the absolute component is the same size

checks.name: wcc_fraction
checks.source: network paper (v630): giant WCC holds 98.8% of neurons

checks.name: mean_undirected_path_wcc
checks.source: network paper (v630): average shortest undirected path in the giant WCC = 3.91 hops
checks.comment: sampled BFS from 1000 sources drawn from the largest weak component

checks.name: mean_directed_path_scc
checks.source: network paper (v630): average shortest directed path in the giant SCC = 4.42 hops

checks.name: max_directed_path_scc
checks.source: network paper (v630): every neuron reachable within 13 hops in the giant SCC
checks.comment: sampled eccentricity, not a full diameter computation

checks.name: in_out_degree_correlation
checks.source: network paper (v630): Pearson R = 0.76, P < 0.001
checks.comment: computed by the gate script over neurons with any connection

checks.name: n_neuropils
checks.source: network paper: 78 anatomically defined brain regions/neuropils
checks.comment: release neuropil labels carry _L/_R hemisphere suffixes (79 distinct labels in v783); the hemisphere-merged count is recorded separately in derived.merged_neuropils

checks.name: rich_club_size_at_degree_37
checks.source: network paper (v630): neurons with total degree > 37 form the rich club, 40,218 neurons (~30%)
checks.comment: counted on the 5-synapse threshold view; v783 has more neurons

checks.name: connection_probability
checks.source: network paper (v630): overall connection probability 0.000161

checks.name: rich_club_connection_probability
checks.source: network paper (v630): connection probability inside the rich club 0.000870

checks.name: rich_club_degree_cutoff_null_normalised
checks.source: network paper (v630): Phi_norm > 1.01 regime spans total degree 37-93, peak at 75
checks.comment: only produced by --heavy; our null uses 3 rewiring reps instead of the paper's 100

checks.name: codex_connection_count
checks.source: codex v783 dataset card
checks.comment: UNRESOLVED CONVENTION - deliberately tight so it reports FAIL: no synapse threshold reproduces 3,732,460 from the v783 release (threshold 4 gives 3,537,227, i.e. 5% below; threshold 5 gives 2,700,513). Recorded so the discrepancy stays visible; the paper's own numbers are the convention we validate against.
